source.title: Understanding Activation Patterns in Artificial Neural Networks by Exploring Stochastic Processes
source.authors: S. Lehmler; Muhammad Saif-ur-Rehman; T. Glasmachers; Ioannis Iossifidis

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains image classifiers on randomized labels and reports training and validation accuracy, but its focus and measures are activation-pattern statistics rather than a direct reproduction of the original generalization experiments.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports accuracy for generalizing and memorizing conditions. These results bear on V1. The paper does not test the other versions. Table 2, Figures 2–6, and Table 5 report activation statistics or process-model analyses, not the claim versions’ outcomes; they are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: Table 1 directly measures random-label training accuracy and held-out validation accuracy after SGD training. This tests V1 using the original kind of manipulation and outcome, although layer freezing and retraining from true-label weights qualify the conditions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' Table 1 interpretation: original-label models generalize, while random-label fitting varies with model, width and training condition. Their main conclusion concerns activation statistics: memorizing layers generally have lower mean firing rates, with weaker separation when earlier layers can memorize, and rapid stabilization during memorization. They do not conclude that every condition perfectly fits random labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses randomized-label memorization as a setup for comparing activation statistics. It grid-searches model and hyperparameter choices, uses SGD with learning rate 0.1, no momentum, batch size 256, and includes layer-freezing memorization conditions; it does not replicate the original settings directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Memorization accuracy varies with dataset, model size, depth, and memorization method; the paper notes weaker separation when all layers can participate in memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean firing rate and related activation statistics distinguish many memorizing and generalizing conditions; separation depends on layer width and whether earlier layers can memorize.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation statistics can indicate random-label memorization under specified layer and training conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation statistics change when training switches from correct to random labels, a switch imposed by the researchers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation dynamics differ between experimentally separated true-label and random-label training phases.

record.problems: The paper selected models and hyperparameters with grid search aimed at finding models able to generalize and memorize; some memorization conditions freeze layers. Training schedule and comparison to true-label training time are not reported as a matched time analysis. Reported accuracy is rounded and no uncertainty estimates are provided for Table 1.
record.rows_left_out: MemRetrainLast rows for Table 1 were omitted to stay within the 60-row limit; the table reports them separately for the same models and datasets. Table 1 is the locator. The paper states that for MLP, MemRetrainAll is identical to MemRetrainLast, so those cases are represented by the MemRetrainAll rows.

untested.parts: A matched training-duration comparison is not established, and CNN/DenseNet MemRetrainAll starts from generalizing weights rather than random initialization. Held-out results are reported as validation accuracy, not explicitly as the benchmark test accuracy.
No time-to-fit comparison or sweep over corruption fractions. The prescribed 10 true-label epochs followed by 100 random-label epochs does not measure relative convergence time.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
No intermediate label-corruption fractions or test-error degradation curve.
No controlled removal or addition of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation.
No measurement of spontaneous real-label-first learning on a mixed noisy dataset. True-label training precedes random-label training by experimental design.

record.verdict_notes: The major extraction error is the MemRetrainAll column alignment: its 12 reported pairs belong to eight CNN and four DenseNet conditions; MLP entries are omitted as identical to MemRetrainLast. Section 3.1.2 explicitly states that all models use the same optimizer and hyperparameters; grid search alone does not establish condition-specific retuning. Architecture/hyperparameter equality concerns comparisons within this study, not equality with the original papers. Omitted CNN/DenseNet MemRetrainLast results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests training on randomized labels and reports training/validation accuracy. It does not establish that the architecture and training hyperparameters were unchanged from the original sources: models and hyperparameters were selected by grid search, and some memorization conditions froze layers.

relationships.condition: Randomly initialized MLPs of width 256 or 512 on MNIST and FashionMNIST
